modes.modes.event.buttons.saved: Callback, URL, web-app and request metadata retained with the message.

modes.modes.event.unscoped.saved: Account-level notice; unknown peer remains explicit.

modes.modes.events.matrix: Event matrix: saved material and remaining unknowns

modes.modes.export.intro: Supply the signed original, an independently retained key fingerprint, the relevant checkpoint and the verification result.
modes.modes.export.title: Hand over a checkable package

modes.modes.flow.caption: Read each observation together with its source identifiers and acquisition record.

modes.modes.hash.changed: Record 2 changed. Its hash no longer matches the saved hash or the link retained by record 3.
modes.modes.hash.intro: The next record keeps the previously saved link. Changing the text changes record 2’s calculated hash.
modes.modes.hash.label: Text of record 2
modes.modes.hash.limit: This sample calculates hashes, not signatures. The real verifier checks every signature and link against the trusted key.
modes.modes.hash.ok: The calculated hash matches the saved hash. The three links agree.
modes.modes.hash.static: Static example: h2 covers “Meet at 11:00”. Changing that text changes h2; record 3 still references the saved h2.
modes.modes.hash.title: Try changing record 2
modes.modes.hash.unavailable: Interactive hashing is unavailable. The static explanation remains readable.
modes.modes.intro: TgWitness records what the connected account observes. A third party can verify the record’s integrity against an independently trusted key.
modes.modes.level.boundary.mechanism: Checkpoint at startup, every 5 minutes by default, and orderly stop. Keep a copy elsewhere.
modes.modes.level.boundary.proves: The later export agrees with an earlier retained length and head; rollback can be detected.
modes.modes.level.container.mechanism: manifest.json lists file hashes; manifest.sig signs it. media.saved binds attachment bytes to an event.
modes.modes.level.container.proves: The supplied files agree with the signed manifest and media receipts.
modes.modes.level.provenance.mechanism: Signed run receipt: source hashes, dependency versions and process context. Self-reported.
modes.modes.level.provenance.proves: What the signing collector reported about its own execution.
modes.modes.level.record.mechanism: SHA-256 chain + Ed25519 per event; the first previous_hash is 64 zeroes.
modes.modes.level.record.proves: Ordering and signatures under the pinned collector key.
modes.modes.level.replica.mechanism: S3-compatible copy encrypted with AES-256-GCM; Object Lock when the bucket supports it.
modes.modes.level.replica.proves: Restore publishes files only after journal, checkpoint and preserved-media verification succeeds.
modes.modes.level.time.mechanism: Evidence mode sends a checkpoint SHA-256 to RFC 3161 authorities (FreeTSA, DigiCert) and OpenTimestamps calendars.
modes.modes.level.time.proves: A verified TSA response dates those bytes; a confirmed OpenTimestamps proof anchors them to Bitcoin.
modes.modes.level.witness.mechanism: Separate host, scoped read-only endpoint, fresh challenge, its own key/journal and TGW1 channel posts.
modes.modes.level.witness.proves: Earlier accepted heads; statuses ok, key_changed, rollback, fork, invalid and no_response.

home.home.nav.label: Page sections
home.home.gh.title1: Nothing to install. No server of yours.
home.home.gh.lead: The simplest way to capture a chat or a whole account. Fork TgWitness, start the capture workflow and sign in: a disposable GitHub runner with a fresh Telegram session exports what you chose and hands you an encrypted archive with GitHub's attestation. The machine that collected it was never yours, so nobody has to trust you or your computer.
home.home.gh.scene: Animation: a fork starts a fresh GitHub runner, a new Telegram session signs in, the chat or account is exported, and the archive comes out attested by GitHub and encrypted to your key.
home.home.gh.s1.text: Your fork runs the pinned workflow from the TgWitness repository.
home.home.gh.s2.text: A disposable GitHub machine with fresh storage. No panel is exposed.
home.home.gh.s3.text: Sign in by QR code or phone. Session imports are not allowed.
home.home.gh.s4.text: Telegram Takeout or the regular API for the account, or one chat's event journal.
home.home.gh.s5.text: GitHub attests the archive. Only the key made in your browser opens it.
home.home.gh.f1.text: The capture helper is a web page and the collector runs on GitHub. No server, no local setup, no session file to hand over.
home.home.gh.f2: A chat or the whole account
home.home.gh.f2.text: All accessible chats or a selection, with dates, chat types and attachment rules — or one chat's event journal.
home.home.gh.f3.text: The verifier checks the archive against GitHub's attestation, the approved workflow and the collector commit. The operator's computer is out of the picture.
home.home.gh.note: Preview. A run lasts 30, 60 or 120 minutes including sign-in, and Telegram may hold a Takeout export for approval. Normal completion logs the temporary session out.
home.home.ticker.label: Built-in protections
home.home.stats.strengths: strengths, read from the source code
home.home.story.title1: We needed one closed chat preserved.
home.home.story.title2: Nothing we found could be checked.
home.home.story.lead: It started with a closed chat run by scammers and one question: how do you preserve it lawfully, in a form that someone who does not trust you can still check?
home.home.story.c1.title: Telegram signs nothing.
home.home.story.c1.text: Nothing shows what a chat contained before a message was edited or deleted. A Desktop export carries only the current versions, and its files can be changed afterwards while the client still shows the original.
home.home.story.c2.title: Every workaround asked for trust.
home.home.story.c2.text: Browser extensions, scripts and copied exports can be altered on the fly, and the recipient has to believe whoever ran them. Signing an already altered export only preserves the alteration.
home.home.story.c3.title: A screenshot holds until it is disputed.
home.home.story.c3.text: If the other side admits it, a screenshot is enough. If they deny it, nothing in it shows it was not made in a minute — and the truth it showed is lost with it.
home.home.story.c4.title: So we built the simplest thing that holds.
home.home.story.c4.text: Sign each record at the moment of capture, link it to the one before, fix the time outside the machine and ship an open verifier. Then we attacked it ourselves — editing, swapping and rolling back records — and closed what we found.
home.home.story.c5.title: Trust moves off you.
home.home.story.c5.text: Out of the box it holds without any server. On a disposable GitHub runner or a sealed Intel TDX machine on Phala, whoever disputes a record has to explain how GitHub, Intel's attestation, the time stamp authorities and Bitcoin all got it wrong.
home.home.story.not.title: Not a surveillance tool
home.home.story.not.text: There are far simpler tools for spying. TgWitness signs its own operator's actions, can keep collection strictly inside the chosen chats, and turns misuse into a matter of record.
home.home.story.privacy.title: Other people's data stays protected
home.home.story.privacy.text: By default a sharing copy pseudonymizes third parties, leaves out media, profiles and contacts, and cannot be made without a stated purpose. Withheld messages leave a signed marker. Pseudonyms are keyed: the key stays encrypted in your vault, so a hidden person can be confirmed when a dispute or a court requires it, and nobody else can reverse it. The signed original stays unchanged.
home.home.story.close: Telegram is a hostile environment: messages are edited, deleted, accounts are banned. None of that changes what was recorded.
home.home.story.note: Theoretical risks exist for every method. The threat model lists what each layer covers and what it does not.
home.home.cmp.lead: A Telegram Desktop export is a folder of files anyone can edit. TgWitness is built for evidence, from the first observation to the hand-over.
home.home.cmp.r2.tw: Observed text and files kept, deletion logged
home.home.cmp.r5.tw: Anyone, offline, with the open-source verifier
home.home.cmp.r6.tw: RFC 3161, Bitcoin and drand time stamps
home.home.cmp.r7.tw: Attested by GitHub or Intel TDX
home.home.cmp.r9.tw: A signed receipt for each press
home.home.cmp.clinic: Tested on the official client: the Export Clinic altered 17 of 45 records, and the export still read like any other.
home.home.hero.lead: Telegram is a hostile environment. TgWitness records what it observed — edits, deletions, gaps — and protects that record from everyone, including the person running it.
home.home.hero.note: No Telegram login needed for the demo
home.home.hero.tip.telegram: Edits, deletes and decides what arrives. Every version and every gap stays on record.
home.home.hero.tip.network: Could change the archive in transit. One changed byte fails verification.
home.home.hero.tip.server: Host staff could touch memory or disk. A sealed Intel TDX machine attests the code that ran.
home.home.hero.tip.operator: Could quietly edit or restore an old copy. The signed hash chain and the rollback record show it.
home.home.hero.tip.clock: A local clock can be set to any date. Outside time stamps fix when the record existed.
home.home.hero.scene: Animation: five threats, Telegram, the network, the server, the operator and the clock, reach for a message and stop at a shield. The message is edited, then deleted, yet both versions and the deletion stay, linked into a signed chain that verifies as valid.
home.home.hero.bad.title: Telegram on its own
home.home.hero.bad.1: Messages are edited and deleted afterwards
home.home.hero.bad.3: A local clock can be set to any date
home.home.hero.good.title: With TgWitness
home.home.hero.good.1: Every observed version and deletion notice is kept
home.home.hero.good.2: A signed, hash-linked journal anyone can verify offline
home.home.hero.good.3: Time fixed by RFC 3161, Bitcoin and drand
home.home.pos.scene: Animation: a scale with Side A and Side B swings back and forth. The line of the record between them does not move.
home.home.pos.l1a: Not a side in the dispute.
home.home.pos.manifest: TgWitness trusts no one and protects only the truth — first of all from the person who runs it.
home.home.pos.manifest2: This is not hostility. It is a guarantee: your record holds for people who have no reason to believe you, and no title, stamp or signature on letterhead can stand in for it.
home.home.pos.l2: Its client is the data — not the user.
home.home.pos.l3: It keeps the inconvenient too: gaps, failures, its own actions.
home.home.zt.lead: Each one is checked by something it doesn't control.
home.home.zt.tg.name: Telegram
home.home.zt.tg.threat: Messages get edited, deleted, history goes missing.
home.home.zt.tg.defense: Every version and every deletion notice is kept. Telegram's update sequence (pts) and message numbers are checked, so a gap is shown instead of hidden.
home.home.zt.op.name: Operator
home.home.zt.op.threat: Even you can't quietly rewrite it.
home.home.zt.op.defense: Every record is signed and linked to the hash of the one before. Restoring an older copy is recorded as a rollback. Panel actions and read receipts sent to the other side are journaled too.
home.home.zt.srv.name: Server
home.home.zt.srv.threat: The machine running it could be compromised.
home.home.zt.srv.defense: Capture on a disposable GitHub runner with an attested archive, or inside an Intel TDX machine whose measured code is attested up to Intel's root.
home.home.zt.clk.name: Clock
home.home.zt.clk.defense: RFC 3161 time stamps, OpenTimestamps anchored in Bitcoin and drand rounds fix the journal in time that nobody on your side controls.
home.home.zt.copy.name: Single copy
home.home.zt.copy.threat: One copy is one point of failure.
home.home.zt.copy.defense: An independent witness on another machine with its own key, signed checkpoints in your Telegram channel through a bot, and an encrypted off-site copy.
home.home.zt.close: No single party has to be trusted. Not Telegram, not the server, not us, not you.
home.home.time.title2: These three would all have to lie together.
home.home.time.lead: Checkpoint hashes are stamped by independent timestamp authorities, anchored in Bitcoin via OpenTimestamps and tied to drand — so anyone can check when a record already existed.
home.home.time.scene: Animation: a checkpoint hash leaves the archive and enters a Bitcoin block through a Merkle tree, an RFC 3161 time stamp authority stamps it, and a drand round pulses below. Three lines converge on the archive: its time is fixed from outside.
home.home.time.byDrand: drand round recorded in the checkpoint
home.home.time.logic: drand shows a checkpoint was signed no earlier than a public round. A time stamp authority and Bitcoin show it existed no later than their time. The record is boxed in from both sides.
home.home.time.note: A timestamp proves when the record existed, not that its content is true.
home.home.secret.lead: Secret chats and self-destructing media are saved as they reach the account. When Telegram's timer runs out, the signed copy stays.
home.home.secret.note: Only secret chats TgWitness starts or accepts (protocol extra, enabled per account), and only what reached the account while it was running.
home.home.secret.scene: Animation: a secret-chat message with a five-second timer self-destructs on the phone. Its pieces fly into the signed journal, which shows it as received, kept and signed.
home.home.modes.lead: Start with a few chats or take the whole account. Load the past, then keep watching.

home.home.modes.m1.text: Follow a few conversations or a Telegram folder, each in its own workspace.
home.home.modes.m2.title: Whole account

home.home.modes.m4.text: A disposable runner captures, hands over an encrypted archive with provenance and disappears.
home.home.levels.title2: Climb only as high as the case demands.
home.home.levels.lead: Each step takes one more party out of the circle of trust. The evidence format stays the same.
home.home.levels.s1.text: Hash chain and Ed25519, checked offline
home.home.levels.s6.text: Measured code, memory sealed from the host
home.home.levels.trust: Parties you still have to trust
home.home.levels.remain: What remains: Intel's attestation root and the cryptography itself.

home.home.uses.j.res: The record remains, with proof it wasn't changed afterwards.
home.home.uses.l.sit: The court needs files it can check.
home.home.uses.l.res: ASiC-E and PAdES files that standard signature validators understand.

home.home.verify.dropHint: or press to run the check

home.home.final.lead: Trust no one. Keep what you saw, and let anyone check it.
